children: shares climbed about 2% as CEO Alex Karp weighed in on how the U.S. should handle legal risks tied to advanced artificial intelligence, according to a CNBC interview.

Karp said AI developers and their customers need workable guardrails because companies could face civil and criminal exposure when systems cause major harm. He argued that firms should disclose potential risks and involve outside oversight when they cannot manage those risks themselves.

The discussion also focused on proprietary business knowledge. Karp said some Palantir customers worry that operational know-how could be absorbed into AI models and later benefit rivals, creating concerns over who bears responsibility for that information.
Karp described the issue as broader than a technology debate, framing it as a societal question. He said companies may need substantial protection from potentially unlimited liability in such cases.

He argued that only the U.S. government could establish a cap and said some businesses could otherwise face pressure to seek government ownership to contain legal exposure. The comments come as debate over AI rules continues in Washington.

title: Palantir Climbs as CEO Sends Blunt Message to AI Industry
